newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BHEL 1st half 96/97 net seen surging - poll.
newsitem.headline: India's BHEL 1st half 96/97 net seen surging - poll.

text.p: India's state-owned Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) is expected to post a 102.5 percent jump in net profit for the first six months ended September 30, 1996, according to a Reuters poll on Tuesday.
"The company's order book position is very healthy.
Improvement in operating profit margins will allow net profit growth to be faster than its turnover growth," said Aditya Srinath, analyst at SSKI Securities, a domestic broker.

The Reuters poll of 14 leading securities firms forecast BHEL's average net profit to rise to 985.6 million rupees ($27.6 million) in first half 1996/97 (April-March) from 486.8 million in the year ago period.
Net sales were expected to rise 22.8 percent to 21,804.9 million rupees in the same six months, it showed.
The poll covered the 30 firms which make up the benchmark Bombay stocks index. BHEL is the country's leading producer of electrical generation equipment.

"We are upgrading BHEL to a buy on the strength of a strong order book -- as Indian power projects come from fully funded IPPs (Independent Power Producers) and not cash-strapped state electricity boards," said analyst Abhijeet Basak of H.G. Asia.
The rise in the firm's order books from a consistent level over the last six months is expected to add to the company's bottomline in the next few years, analysts said.
They estimated BHEL to have an order book position of over one billion rupees as of date.
"The effect will be felt on the turnover and profits over the next two years," H.G. Asia's Basak said in a note to investors.
The forecast for BHEL's average net profit ranged from a high of 1,500 million rupees to a low of 700.0 million rupees.
"We are expecting a 20 percent growth in sales," said analyst Prabodh Agarwal of James Capel B&K.
"The emerging power scenario and industrial growth will provide enough growth opportunities for BHEL," Agarwal said.
